transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Time: 08:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood Solutions), Diane Kwan (Sentinel Head of ML), Ravi Menon (Sentinel Product), Jia Lee (Sentinel Eng Lead), Omar Salim (Sentinel Security), Tom (Sentinel Scribe)

Summary:
Brief: Kickoff to align on POC acceptance criteria: quality eval plan (golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks), workload sizing and bench targets, timeline and deliverables. Goal: define measurable acceptance thresholds and who owns artifacts.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria (accuracy/format/hallucination thresholds, latency SLOs)
- Golden prompts and negative/edge-case examples
- Regression suite and scoring rubric (weighted metrics)
- Workload sizing: tokens, concurrency, sequences per second, typical prompt lengths
- Bench plan: smoke, soak, and canary for dedicated vs hosted variants
- Security gating: data retention, KMS, SOC2 artifacts, SSO
- Timeline: 6-week POC with phased checkpoints

Action items (short): see metadata block above.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Alyssa Chen: hi everyone, thanks for joining. we'll run for about 50-ish minutes, goal is to get to a crisp acceptance criteria and who does what. um Marco will cover benching approach, i'll cover the eval rubric and golden prompts.
[00:00:18] Diane Kwan: thanks Alyssa, appreciate it. quick context: Sentinel AI is integrating LLM summarization and classification into our incident triage flow. main worries: hallucinations, structured output format, and hitting sub-400ms token latency end-to-end.
[00:00:36] Ravi Menon: and from product side we need precision on high-confidence labels for triage routing, so false positives are more expensive than false negatives for us. timeline wise we're hoping a pilot in prod by end of Q3.
[00:00:50] Marco Ruiz: got it. when you say sub-400ms token latency, is that 400ms per token or 400ms tail for a 200-token response?
[00:00:58] Diane Kwan: good callout — we mean 95th p99-ish for 100-token responses end-to-end, so maybe around 500-600ms p95 is acceptable if the average is lower. we can be flexible if quality wins.
[00:01:12] Marco Ruiz: ok that helps. we'll prototype both hosted and dedicated slugs — dedicated for predictable throughput if you want lower tail latency. note: quantized variants can shave cost at some accuracy tradeoff, we'll test those.
[00:01:28] Jia Lee: curious about KV cache and prefix caching you mentioned in docs — will that help cold-starts for conversational contexts?
[00:01:35] Marco Ruiz: yes, Redwood's runtime caches KV state for repeated prefixes which reduces compute for repeated prompts; but we'll need to see your prompt overlap rates. if prompts vary a lot benefit is smaller.
[00:01:46] Tom (Scribe): [inaudible]
[00:01:48] Alyssa Chen: high level on acceptance criteria — we propose a two-track gate: quality (accuracy, hallucination, format correctness) and performance (latency, error rate, throughput). both must be met to pass POC.
[00:02:02] Diane Kwan: can you put numbers on those? what do you recommend for hallucination/format thresholds?
[00:02:08] Alyssa Chen: from similar customers we recommend: hallucination rate < 2% on golden set (when a model invents facts or claims outside provided context), format validity > 98% for structured outputs (e.g., JSON fields present + schema validation), and a quality score (see rubric) of > 0.82 weighted F1 across classes. these are starting points, we can tune.
[00:02:28] Ravi Menon: how do you measure hallucination? automated checks or human label?
[00:02:34] Marco Ruiz: mix — we run automated heuristics (fact checks against indexed doc set, citations, impossible dates) then human spot checks on a 200-item golden set. for POC we usually do 200 golden prompts with about 20 targeted edge-cases focusing on hallucination-prone queries.
[00:02:52] Diane Kwan: we can do that. we'll pull 200 examples from our anonymized incidents and flag 30 critical-edge cases.
[00:02:58] Alyssa Chen: perfect. on regression testing: we supply a historical set of inputs (golden prompts) and an automated scoring pipeline that computes multiple metrics — accuracy, hallucination flag, format pass, response length distribution, and per-class recall/precision. we weight them: accuracy 40%, hallucination 30%, format 20%, latency 10% — suggested.
[00:03:20] Omar Salim: security questions — is any customer text persisted in Redwood logs? we need to know retention and options for disabling retention or sending over VPC-only private deployment.
[00:03:28] Priya Patel: quick answer: hosted mode keeps logs for troubleshooting but you can request redaction or opt for dedicated/private where data plane stays in your VPC. we'll provide SOC2 artefacts and KMS integration for encryption at rest in Private.
[00:03:41] Omar Salim: good, please send SOC2 and SAML docs. also must confirm HSM/KMS for key management — we'll need that for procurement.
[00:03:50] Alyssa Chen: action: we'll include SOC2 summary and our KMS integration doc in the packet.
[00:03:55] Jia Lee: for benching — Marco can you outline the workload sizing we should plan for? tokens per month, concurrency?
[00:04:02] Marco Ruiz: sure. tell me your expected qps for the triage pipeline and average prompt/response length.
[00:04:07] Ravi Menon: during peak we expect 28 requests/sec, average prompt 30 tokens, average response 150 tokens. so roughly 28 * (30+150) = 5040 tokens/sec peak, about 15M tokens/day, ~450M tokens/month. that's ballpark.
[00:04:26] Marco Ruiz: ok that maps to medium-heavy workload. for POC bench we'll run three phases: a smoke test (10 minutes, small sample), an acceptance bench (targeted 10k requests across sizes to validate p95 latency and error rates), and a soak (24h at ~60% peak) to check stability. we'll provide a harness and ask you run one soak in your environment and one on Redwood hosted/dedicated.
[00:04:47] Diane Kwan: sounds reasonable. what are error rate SLOs?
[00:04:51] Marco Ruiz: target error rate < 0.5% for 95% of runs, and no >1% sustained spikes. fallback rules: if model falls below quality threshold we'll auto-route to a safer model or stub with degradation message.
[00:05:04] Alyssa Chen: back to golden prompts — we recommend 200 canonical prompts broken into: 120 common cases, 60 edge/ambiguous, 20 hallucination traps. each prompt should include a ground-truth expected output (for structured outputs a JSON schema) and a pass/fail rubric.
[00:05:20] Ravi Menon: will the golden prompts include doc-context retrieval cases? our triage depends on attached logs.
[00:05:25] Marco Ruiz: yes include retrieval contexts; we'll test with and without retrieval to observe hallucination delta. for retrieval we'll connect your vector store or supply a simulated docset.
[00:05:36] Jia Lee: for local benchmarking we will need a Dockerized harness and some scripts — can Redwood provide those?
[00:05:40] Marco Ruiz: yes we'll hand over an open-source harness (small modifications to fit your auth), plus a set of scripts to run loads and produce the metrics CSV. also a small example of the Redwood Console dashboards you'll get.
[00:05:52] Tom (Scribe): note: Marco to provide harness repo link.
[00:05:56] Alyssa Chen: scoring approach detail: we'll compute per-example score from components: content correctness (0-1), hallucination penalty (-1 to 0), format pass (0 or 1). aggregate using weighted mean. also compute A/B delta for each model variant. we'll share a spreadsheet template.
[00:06:14] Diane Kwan: can you demonstrate the scoring on a toy example?
[00:06:18] Alyssa Chen: sure — example: Input: incident digest -> Expected: JSON {priority:high, owner:infra, summary:...}. Model output matches keys but invents owner as "third-party" -> content correctness 0.6, hallucination penalty -0.5, format pass 1, weighted score = 0.6*0.4 + (-0.5)*0.3 + 1*0.2... math gives a pass/fail threshold. we'll send calc in sheet.
[00:06:40] Ravi Menon: regarding regression: how often will we run it? on every model change?
[00:06:46] Marco Ruiz: recommended cadence: every model version release and daily/weekly quick smoke runs. for POC we'll run nightly regression with human spot checks twice a week.
[00:06:57] Omar Salim: procurement: we'll need a document mapping controls to our vendor risk matrix. is that standard?
[00:07:03] Priya Patel: yes we'll include a vendor controls mapping and a short runbook for audit.
[00:07:08] Alyssa Chen: timeline proposal: 6-week POC broken into phases: week 0 (setup & creds), week 1 (golden set collection & rubric alignment), weeks 2-3 (bench & quality runs), week 4 (soak & regression), week 5 (tuning and final acceptance), week 6 (handoff + production runbook). we can compress to 4 weeks if Sentinel provides artifacts quickly.
[00:07:28] Diane Kwan: our org calendar fits 6 weeks better. we can commit to providing the sample data in week 0.
[00:07:35] Alyssa Chen: great. risk register quick list: (1) data privacy/PII in examples -> mitigate with redaction & VPC/private, (2) hallucination high on retrieval-free prompts -> mitigate with retrieval and prompt engineering, (3) latency spikes -> mitigate with dedicated lanes and autoscaling / warm pools.
[00:07:52] Ravi Menon: any recommended prompt engineering patterns for reducing hallucination?
[00:07:56] Marco Ruiz: use constrained output schemas, explicit "do not invent" instructions, and include short citations or evidence context. also use shorter decoding temperatures for classification.
[00:08:07] Jia Lee: for integration, what SDKs? we use Python microservices and some Node for routing.
[00:08:11] Priya Patel: Redwood supports Python and Node SDKs, plus a simple REST API. we'll include code snippets for streaming and structured output validation.
[00:08:20] Diane Kwan: can you do a quick sketch of the final acceptance checklist?
[00:08:23] Alyssa Chen: yes — final acceptance checklist (proposed):
- Quality gate: weighted score >= 0.82 on golden set; hallucination < 2%; format validation pass >=98%
- Performance gate: p95 latency <= 600ms for 100-token responses; error rate <0.5%
- Security gate: SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration verified for private, SAML SSO tested
- Operational gate: runbooks for rollbacks, pen tests scheduled, SLA terms agreed

[00:08:54] Omar Salim: add to security gate: log-retention policy and ability to purge customer data on demand.
[00:08:58] Alyssa Chen: noted.
[00:09:01] Tom (Scribe): [typing]
[00:09:03] Marco Ruiz: two more technical notes: (1) we recommend capturing KV cache hit rates during soak to understand savings and (2) measure token emission variance — long tails can push up cost.
[00:09:14] Diane Kwan: agreed.
[00:09:16] Alyssa Chen: ok wrapping — recap of next steps: Alyssa sends golden prompt template + rubric and harness link; Diane sends 200 sample queries + 30 edge cases; Marco & Jia schedule bench run; Omar will send security checklist. we'll aim to reconvene after initial bench (target 2025-05-30).
[00:09:36] Diane Kwan: thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[00:09:39] Alyssa Chen: thanks, talk soon.
[00:09:41] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription glitches (names, acronyms) present, some speaker labels merged. The audio had a brief dropout around 00:01:46.
